commands: For disposable probe tests, record and run the actual fully qualified class/method filters under their module Gradle test tasks, with -Ptests.seed=17764C0DE and --rerun-tasks; record any packaged-distribution build and real startup commands.
environment: Linux, JDK 21, isolated disposable checkout. Verify remote head; obtain canonical claim and host locks. This exploratory probe is independent of the existing exact-head regression gate. Do not push a source branch or post public comments.
head: d88ae0c6269e067602a90ed8e655df275f6f42f7
requirements: Prototype only in the disposable checkout. Jetty 12.1.14 GracefulHandler.handleShutdownRejection runs before delegation; inject a distinctive marker solely there. Demonstrate over a real HTTP connection that a post-shutdown request receives the marker and does not enter the wrapped Solr handler, while an in-flight request completes or has its real failure reported. Verify an ordinary Solr-generated 503 and an unmarked Jetty/proxy 503 do not receive the marker. Preserve server/client logs and response headers. Test the packaged server startup XML/classpath as well as JettySolrRunner: server/build.gradle currently disables Java compilation and webapp classes are not automatically Jetty startup classes. Record exact packaging changes or prove infeasibility.

Implement the smallest disposable client prototype needed to carry the signal through both JDK and Jetty HTTP clients and retry only the rejected LBSolrClient subrequest on a different suitable endpoint when its body is demonstrably repeatable. Exercise a real two-node/multi-shard scenario with a non-idempotent atomic increment: one shard or phase succeeds before another is rejected, final persisted values show each intended increment exactly once, and no completed shard request is resent. Repeat with no viable alternate endpoint and assert failure without whole-batch replay. Record wire/request counts and stored values. Include sync and async behavior or explicitly mark any untested path incomplete.

Test an UpdateRequest with a one-shot document iterator and an opaque streaming update whose bodies have begun consumption. Neither may be retried unless the probe demonstrates a sound replay contract; assert no silently shortened successful replay. Test missing marker, an ordinary application 503 after a partial update, V2 skipRetry, mixed-version unmarked server, and a proxy/header-modification case or document the exact supported direct-node trust boundary and inability to establish intermediary provenance. Do not infer safety from HTML, status alone, or generic Retry-After.

The current outer CloudSolrClient treats RequestNotSentException as a communication error and may replay an entire batch; existing RouteException 503 retry also replays it. Do not simply map the new signal to either existing whole-request retry. Prove the failed-subrequest and exhaustion paths preserve already completed work. Explicitly report pre-existing replay paths and whether the prototype changes them.

SOLR-18341 is related pending work. Do not assume all apparent set/delete operations are safe under concurrent writes, or copy its classification without analysis. Report exactly which request forms and network topologies the probe covers, what remains ambiguous, and whether the original in-flight Solr 503 case remains unresolved. Report a recommendation for a narrowly scoped production change only if the real-boundary evidence supports it.

Record the unchanged-head baseline and each actual command, exit code, test count, fresh XML, logs, wire evidence and disposable patch; compile or setup errors, skipped tests, fabricated markers without their origin, and mock-only assertions do not establish end-to-end safety. Publish a passed, failed, incomplete, or non-reproduced receipt as appropriate and release only with verified executor-stop evidence.
